thread:
jess: Heads-up — doing a quick spike on per-org noisy-neighbor detection for the console. Goal: surface a single signal we can show on customer dashboards that combines throughput, queue depth, and error spikes. Thinking name: noisy_neighbor_index (NNI).

mario: +1 on a single index. Question: where should runtime emit the inputs? We can easily emit per-request labels but worried about cardinality.

ashley: UI requirement: no PII. Whatever we surface must be groupable by org_id (hashed) + friendly name from billing. Also need a quick drilldown to recent traces.

dataplatform: ingestion constraints: Prometheus is ok for short windows but we need high-res (1s) for burst detection and 90d retention for historical patterns. Suggest ingest raw counters into TSDB (prometheus remote write -> clickhouse) and export derived NNI as a rollup metric.

mario: runtime note: we can emit these metrics with labels: {org_id, model_variant, route, instance_type}. Example metric:
```
redwood.infer.kv_cache_miss_total{org_id="<hashed>",route="/api/v1/gen",model="rw-large-v1"}
```
But we should limit labels to avoid explosion. Maybe drop model_variant on low-volume orgs.

jess: Good. For NNI calculation proposal (draft): normalize per-org token/sec over 1m, queue_depth 95th percentile over 1m, and error_rate spikes (5m). Weighted sum: 0.5*norm_tokens + 0.3*norm_queue + 0.2*norm_errors. Then categorize into levels: green/yellow/red.

ashley: UX: show level + small sparkline + button: "Open tenant timeline". On hover show contributing factors (tokens 1m, q95, err 5m). Keep color blind friendly palette.

dataplatform: Implementation details — we should precompute NNI in backend every 30s and store as `redwood.tenant.nni{org_id=...,window="30s"}`. Dashboards can query that instead of computing client-side. We'll also write a derivation job pseudo-config:
```
job: tenant_nni_rollup
input: token_rate_1m, queue_q95_1m, error_rate_5m
output: tenant_nni_30s
retention: 90d
```

mario: A couple of caveats from runtime: to compute token_rate per org we need request attribution before batching. We batch many orgs together; we can still attribute tokens back using org_id in request metadata, but it adds a tiny CPU cost. Is that acceptable?

eng-plat-lead: We should measure cost. If attribution adds >5% CPU on inference path it's a no-go. Can we do sampling? Maybe emit per-batch totals and apportion by count of requests per org in the batch — that still reveals noisy orgs.

mario: Apportionment is possible and cheaper. We'll prototype both: exact attribution and apportionment estimate. Flag: apportionment loses precision for multi-tenant heavy batches.

jess: Alerting policy: propose we create an anomaly alert when NNI > 0.8 for 10m OR sudden delta >0.5 within 5m. Those should trigger a noisy-neighbor investigation runbook (link). For enterprise customers we can auto-suggest mitigation: route affinity or quota bump request page.

ashley: Rollout UX: gated feature flag + 2-step rollout. 1) internal only; 2) opt-in for 10 pilot customers; 3) auto-suggest for top 50 customers with dedicated billing contacts. Console should surface why NNI is high and recommended actions.

dataplatform: Data privacy: in hosted mode we can show org_name; in private deployments we must honor local naming. We'll add a label `display_name_source` and UI picks appropriately.

sre-bot: INCIDENT BOT: Created alert template `noisy_neighbor_high` -> pager: oncall-eng-platform, severity: P2, runbook: /runbooks/noisy-neighbor.md

eng-plat-lead: Next steps: mario + dataplatform to submit an ingestion design doc (2 pages) by EOD Friday. jess + ashley will draft console mockups and the rollout plan. We'll meet Tue 10am to decide thresholds and canary groups.

mario: I'll also attach prototype metrics export (small trace) to the doc. If apportionment looks good we can avoid heavy runtime work.

jess: thanks — appreciate quick turn. If anyone has objections to NNI formula speak now. Otherwise I'll add this thread to the design doc.

ashley: no objections from me. small ask: add a keyboard-shortcut to open "tenant timeline" — power users will love it. :keyboard:

dataplatform: noted. I'll include retention/cost estimates in the doc.

jess: done for now. Will ping again after design doc draft is up.
